theory.what: Alerting notifies NOC staff when metrics exceed defined thresholds.
theory.why: Without alerting, issues go unnoticed until users complain.
theory.how: Define thresholds: Warning 70%, Critical 90%. Channels: email, Slack, PagerDuty.
theory.when: Set alerts for all critical infrastructure. Tune to reduce false positives.
theory.configuration:
# Prometheus alert
- alert: HighCPU
  expr: node_cpu_usage > 90
  for: 5m

theory.what: Structured process for detecting, classifying, and resolving network incidents.
theory.why: Without process, incidents are handled inconsistently leading to longer outages.
theory.how: Lifecycle: Detection → Classification (P1-P4) → Notification → Investigation → Resolution → Post-mortem.
theory.when: Follow for every incident. P1/P2 require immediate response.
theory.configuration:
# Severity levels
P1: Total outage (respond immediately)
P2: Major degradation (respond <15min)
P3: Minor impact (respond <1hr)
P4: Informational

theory.what: Formal process for planning, approving, and implementing network changes.
theory.why: Uncontrolled changes are the #1 cause of outages.
theory.how: Process: Request → Review (CAB) → Schedule → Implement → Verify → Close.
theory.when: Every network change goes through this process.
theory.configuration:
# Change types
Standard: Pre-approved, low risk
Normal: CAB approval required
Emergency: Expedited, post-review

theory.what: Systematic investigation to identify the fundamental cause of an incident.
theory.why: Fixing symptoms without root cause means problems recur.
theory.how: Methods: 5 Whys, Fishbone diagram, Timeline analysis, Fault tree.
theory.when: Perform RCA for every P1/P2 incident.
theory.configuration:
# 5 Whys Example
1. Why outage? Core switch failed
2. Why? CPU 100%
3. Why? STP loop
4. Why? Unauthorized switch
5. Root cause: No port security

theory.what: Service Level Agreements define measurable targets for availability and performance.
theory.why: SLAs set expectations and drive investment decisions.
theory.how: Metrics: 99.9% (8.76hr downtime/yr), 99.99% (52.6min/yr). MTTR, latency, packet loss.
theory.when: Define SLAs for all critical services. Monitor continuously.
theory.configuration:
# SLA targets
99.9% = 8.76 hours downtime/year
99.99% = 52.6 minutes/year
99.999% = 5.26 minutes/year

theory.what: Maintaining accurate documentation of topology, configs, IPs, and procedures.
theory.why: Without docs, troubleshooting takes longer and DR is impossible.
theory.how: Essential: Network diagrams, IPAM, device inventory, config backups, SOPs, runbooks.
theory.when: Document everything. Update on every change. Review quarterly.
theory.configuration:
# Tools
- NetBox (IPAM + inventory)
- draw.io (diagrams)
- Oxidized (config backup)
- Wiki (procedures)

theory.what: Establishing normal metrics to detect anomalies and plan capacity.
theory.why: Without baselines, you cannot distinguish normal from abnormal.
theory.how: Process: Identify metrics → Collect 30+ days → Calculate avg/peak/95th → Document → Set thresholds.
theory.when: Baseline all critical links. Use 95th percentile for capacity planning.
theory.configuration:
# Key metrics to baseline
- WAN utilization (bps)
- Router CPU/memory
- Interface errors
- Latency

theory.what: Open-source visualization platform for real-time monitoring dashboards.
theory.why: Dashboards provide at-a-glance visibility into network health.
theory.how: Components: Data sources (Prometheus, InfluxDB), Panels (graphs, gauges), Variables, Alerts.
theory.when: Create dashboards for: NOC overview, per-site status, WAN health.

theory.what: Open-source monitoring with pull-based collection, time-series storage, and PromQL.
theory.how: Architecture: Server (scrapes), Exporters (expose metrics), PromQL (query), Alertmanager (alerts).
theory.when: Use for server, container, and network monitoring (via SNMP exporter).
theory.configuration:
# prometheus.yml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: network
    static_configs:
      - targets: [snmp-exporter:9116]

theory.what: Enterprise monitoring supporting SNMP, agents, and custom checks with built-in alerting.
theory.why: Widely used in enterprise NOCs for comprehensive monitoring.
theory.how: Components: Server, Agent, Proxy, Templates, Triggers, Actions.
theory.when: Use for enterprise network and server monitoring.

theory.what: Open-source network monitoring with auto-discovery, alerting, and SNMP polling.
theory.why: Free alternative to commercial NMS with strong community support.
theory.how: Features: Auto-discovery, SNMP polling, alerting, API, plugins, distributed polling.
theory.when: Use LibreNMS for budget-friendly network monitoring with good SNMP support.

theory.what: Open-source IP address management and data center infrastructure management tool.
theory.why: Single source of truth for network documentation — IPs, devices, circuits, racks.
theory.how: Features: IPAM, device inventory, rack layouts, circuits, VLANs, API, webhooks, custom fields.
theory.when: Use NetBox as the authoritative source for all network documentation.
